properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Indiana...

Wabash River from Montezuma through Mount Carmel.

White River from Edwardsport through Hazleton.

.Minor flooding continues along the White River from Edwardsport
downriver with the crest already past Hazleton.  Minor flooding also
continues on the Wabash River from Montezuma down to Mount Carmel
with the crest approaching Vincennes. Rain amounts with scattered
storms Wednesday evening are not expected to impact main stem river
levels.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Wabash River at Mount Carmel.

* WHEN...Until late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...At 20.0 feet, River is bankfull in all locations.  All
oil field production ceases with the exception of pumping units on
substructures.  Access to these are by boat only.  Agricultural
losses increase dramatically.  Farmers move livestock to higher
ground.  City of Mount Carmel leaves flood gates B and C in year
round.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:45 PM CDT /1:45 PM EDT/ Tuesday the stage was 19.8 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 12:45 PM CDT /1:45 PM EDT/ Tuesday was 19.8 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 20.2 feet
early Thursday afternoon. It will then fall below flood stage
Saturday afternoon.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/ind.

/1100 AM EDT/.

SVRTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
Northwestern Decatur County in southwestern Georgia...
Miller County in southwestern Georgia...
Southwestern Mitchell County in southwestern Georgia...
Southwestern Baker County in southwestern Georgia...
Northeastern Seminole County in southwestern Georgia...
East central Early County in southwestern Georgia...

* Until 1115 PM EDT.

* At 1026 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm was located over Colquitt,
moving south at 15 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Colquitt, Bainbridge, Damascus, Brinson, Hanover, Ausmac, Babcock,
Eldorendo, Decatur Co A/P, Steinham Store, Boykin, Cyrene,
Enterprise, Harmony Church Rd/hwy 45, Cooktown, Jeterville,
Bellview, Bethany, and Mimsville.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Large hail, damaging wind, and continuous cloud to ground lightning
are occurring with this storm. Move indoors immediately. Lightning is
one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can hear thunder,
you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with this storm, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued August 25 at 9:23PM CDT until August 25 at 10:00PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX
properties.description:
At 923 PM CDT, automated weather equipment reported severe
thunderstorms were located along a line extending from near New
Mobeetie to 6 miles southwest of Lake Mcclellan to 12 miles east of
Wayside, moving southeast at 45 mph.

HAZARD...70 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Automated weather equipment.

IMPACT...Expect some tree damage. Damage is likely to mobile homes,
roofs, and outbuildings.

Locations impacted include...
Pampa, Clarendon, Shamrock, Claude, Miami, White Deer, Mclean, Groom,
Lefors, Howardwick, Hedley, Lelia Lake, Lake Mcclellan, Wayside,
Goodnight, Kingsmill, Dozier, Alanreed, Codman, and Greenbelt Lake.
properties.instruction:
For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.

Torrential rainfall is occurring with these storms, and may lead to
flash flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued August 25 at 9:26PM CDT until August 25 at 11:30PM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX
properties.description:
At 926 PM CDT, emergency management reports multiple stranded
vehicles due to water over roadways. Between 0.5 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Emergency management reported.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Amarillo, Mescalero Park and Bushland.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
